title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County are suing the city of Española after a July 23 traffic stop. Jaclynn Gonzales, 21, was driving with her 12-year-old sister when a Flock Safety camera misread their license plate, confusing a final 2 for a 7 and flagging the car as stolen from Rio Rancho. Police stopped them on Calle Duran, handcuffed both sisters, and placed them in separate patrol cars before realizing the error. Jaclynn asked officers to call their mother, who lived nearby, to pick up the girl, but officers instead handcuffed the child and put her in another police vehicle.

The sisters filed separate lawsuits on January 3 in state District Court, seeking unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, worry, and restriction of movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, also represents Adam Pacheco, a 17-year-old honor student who was forced to kneel in the road after being mistakenly targeted as an armed robbery suspect in a separate case. The city of Española, Police Chief Mizel A. Garcia, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. The lawsuits are now pending in court.
